credits.text: Phrases from the FSI Amharic Basic Course (public domain), Wikivoyage contributors "Amharic phrasebook", and Omniglot; native-speaker review pending.

activities.prompt: Hanna stops at a small café (buna bet) in Addis Ababa.

activities.speaker: Waiter
activities.translation: It's nearby. It's on your right

task.feedbackCorrect: Right: Siga albelam — I don't eat meat.
task.feedbackIncorrect: Melkam migib wishes someone a good meal, and Sint new? asks a price.
task.prompt: The waiter recommends doro wet (chicken stew), but you don't eat meat. What do you say?

activities.prompt: Order a coffee aloud, then ask how much it is.

lessons.objective: Follow Hanna ordering coffee and asking the way, then choose how to decline meat.
lessons.title: At the buna bet

examples: Kirb new (It's nearby) / RuK new (It's far)
Fitlefit new (It's in front of you)
activities.explanation: New at the end of these phrases works like 'it is': put the description first. The same word ends the price question and your name.

task.feedbackIncorrect: The description comes first, new last.

lessons.objective: Notice how many short answers end in new (it is), then build two.
lessons.title: It is …: sentences ending in new

activities.speaker: Story
activities.text: Dawit is meeting Hanna for coffee but cannot find the café. He asks a shopkeeper:

activities.speaker: Story
activities.text: He finds Hanna already eating bread with her coffee. He says:

task.feedbackIncorrect: Look at the shopkeeper's last line.
task.prompt: Is the café far from the shop?

task.feedbackIncorrect: Listen again and check the transcript.

activities.translation: Where? / It's nearby / Enjoy your meal
activities.unavailableReason: There is no genuine recording of these lines yet. Root will not stand in a synthetic or unrelated voice, so this listening step opens once a real speaker has recorded it. The story and its question above count on their own.
